title: A Prom for the Homecoming
premise: Jude Quintana has spent three years at Ashgrove Academy keeping their head down, counting the days until a scholarship-funded escape. When their best friend Priya vanishes days before Homecoming, leaving only her dorm keys and a cryptic note about 'the second championship,' Jude discovers the academy's beloved traditions mask an old-money society that trades favors, futures, and sometimes people. To find Priya, Jude must enter both the rowing championship and the secret 'Founders' Court' contest that decides which student the elite will sponsor — or destroy. Winning both means betraying the found family Jude has built along the way; in the end, Jude wins neither on the school's terms, exposes the society's ledger of debts, and brings Priya home, choosing love and loyalty over the prize that was never really theirs to want.
about_author: Felix Ishikawa is the pen name of a former boarding-school scholarship kid who writes about institutions from the inside out. They live near water, row badly, and believe every academy has at least one locked door worth opening.

chapters.title: Ninety-Seven Days
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Opening day of senior spring at Ashgrove Academy: Jude catalogs the social hierarchy, their scholarship obligations, and the countdown to graduation. Establishes Priya as the one person who makes the place bearable. Emotional beat: weary resignation shot through with quiet affection.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Coach Okafor strong-arms Jude onto the varsity crew despite their refusal to care about sports. A humiliating first practice reveals unexpected aptitude — and the team's wary welcome from roommate Theo and stroke-seat Marisol. Emotional beat: reluctant belonging beginning to take root.

chapters.title: Keys
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Priya misses their weekly diner ritual, then misses class, then is simply gone. Her dorm key sits in an envelope labeled with Jude's name and two words: 'second championship.' Administration shrugs; her parents are oddly calm. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: Invisible No More
chapters.summary: Alternating Jude/Theo POV. Jude and Theo start pulling threads — Priya's laptop wiped, her research folder on Founders' Court history deleted from the library archive. First hint that faculty are watching them. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening friendship into partnership.

chapters.title: Rowing Toward Nothing
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The crew qualifies for regionals while Jude is distracted; Marisol covers for Jude's lapses but demands honesty in return. Her own scholarship backstory surfaces — she knows what the school does to students who ask questions. Emotional beat: solidarity offered at a price.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In the restricted stacks, Jude finds Priya's hidden notebook: decades of names, debts, and 'sponsorships' — the Founders' Court quietly owns its winners. The 'second championship' is the Court's annual selection ritual held during Homecoming week. Emotional beat: horror reframing everything familiar.

chapters.title: Invitation
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Headmaster Voss personally invites Jude to compete for the Court's 'Founders' Prize,' full ride to any university — the exact future Priya was chasing. The offer is generous, gentle, and unmistakably a leash. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: What Theo Knows
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confesses his older brother won the Prize five years ago and hasn't called home since. He's been competing for the Court hoping to find him. Jude realizes they're not the only one searching. Emotional beat: guilt and shared purpose entwined.

chapters.title: Splits
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Regionals approach; training suffers as Jude investigates. Coach Okafor corners Jude with a warning that sounds like protection but smells like instruction. First real rift with Marisol, who needs this season clean. Emotional beat: the cost of divided loyalty made concrete.

chapters.title: The Court Assembles
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude infiltrates a Court mixer disguised as an alumni gala, witnessing the sponsors appraising students like yearlings. Voss introduces the four finalists — including Jude and Theo. Priya's name appears nowhere, which terrifies more than if it appeared. Emotional beat: gilded menace.

chapters.title: Homecoming Week Begins
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Campus transforms into bunting-and-tradition spectacle while Jude runs double lives: dawn rows, midnight archives. Marisol covers again but gives an ultimatum — be present for finals or don't come back. Emotional beat: love expressed as tough limits.

chapters.title: Priya's Roommate
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A former roommate of Priya's, now graduated and sponsored, meets Jude off-campus and half-confesses: Priya refused the Prize, tried to expose the ledger, and was 'relocated.' There's a facility upstate. Emotional beat: hope arriving wrapped in dread.

chapters.title: Throwing the Race
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo proposes throwing the Court competition so neither of them can be claimed — but the Court punishes refusal by revoking scholarships, and Marisol would pay too. Jude refuses; the argument turns vicious. Emotional beat: the found family fracturing under pressure.

chapters.title: Regionals
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Race day. Exhausted and heartsore, Jude rows the race of their life anyway — for the boat, for Marisol, for the version of themselves that still wanted something simple. They win. It feels like nothing. Emotional beat: hollow triumph.

chapters.title: The Offer Renewed
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Voss, impressed, sweetens the Prize: win Saturday's Court final and Priya's record gets 'cleaned up' — a veiled admission she's alive. Now winning might be the only way to reach her. Emotional beat: the trap closing with a bow on it.

chapters.title: Reconciliation
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol learns what the Prize actually costs and finds Jude on the boathouse roof. They rebuild the plan together: use the final, don't be used by it. Theo rejoins with a map of the Court's records room. Emotional beat: forgiveness as strategy and grace.

chapters.title: Night Before
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Quiet interlude: the trio shares stolen pizza in the empty dining hall, trading fears and promises. Jude admits they stopped counting days somewhere along the way. Emotional beat: tenderness before the storm; the theme of found family at full warmth.

chapters.title: The Second Championship
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The Court final: a staged debate-and-vote ritual before masked sponsors. Jude performs brilliantly, then goes off-script, reading names aloud from the ledger — including Theo's brother's. Chaos erupts; Voss moves to have Jude escorted out. Emotional beat: defiance as climax ignition.

chapters.title: Upstate
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Using the chaos as cover, Theo and Marisol execute the real plan — breaking into the records room and finding the relocation address, while Jude stalls the Court. They confirm Priya is held at the Ashgrove 'study center' upstate. Emotional beat: adrenaline and trust.

chapters.title: Bring Her Home
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. With Coach Okafor — revealed as a former refused finalist — driving, they retrieve Priya. She's shaken but intact, and her evidence plus the ledger go to a journalist ally. Voss's machine begins to crack publicly. Emotional beat: rescue earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Investigations begin; sponsors scatter; scholarships are protected by anonymous alumni who owed Priya. Theo hears his brother's voice on the phone. Marisol captains next year's boat. Jude declines every replacement offer. Emotional beat: consequences rippling outward, justice partial but real.

chapters.title: Prom
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The school holds its rescheduled prom under new scrutiny. Priya, back and furious and laughing, drags everyone onto the floor. Jude dances with no agenda, no countdown — home was never a place to graduate from. Final line echoes the opening count: zero days left, and staying anyway. Emotional beat: love against duty, resolved in joy.
